home.noAgentsTitle: Your machine. Your keys. Your agents.
home.noAgentsSubtitle: Your agents work on their own sandboxed Linux desktops — never on your screen — while you keep using this computer. Their machines, conversations, memory and keys all stay here; nothing leaves except the calls you configure.
home.noProvider: no provider key found — add one to .env or Settings
home.dockerReady: docker · one container per agent, on this computer
home.dockerStopped: docker stopped · starts when an agent needs it
home.dockerNotFound: docker not found — agents can't run code or use a desktop
home.webNotConfigured: firecrawl not configured — agents can't browse the web
home.loopback: bound to loopback · no accounts, no telemetry
home.startWithTeamDesc: Atlas (browser and desktop), Vega (research), Rigel (code) and Lyra (data), together in one squad. Ask the squad anything and they hand it to whoever fits.
home.squadEmpty: A squad puts several agents in one thread. Address any of them, and they delegate to whoever fits the job.

sidebar.newCommits: {count} new commit{count, plural, one {} other {s}} on GitHub — see how to update
sidebar.newVersion: Chuck Bot {version} is out — see how to update
sidebar.squadNeedTwo: Two or more agents can work as a squad.
sidebar.squadGroupAgents: Group agents so they can hand work to each other.
sidebar.deleteThreadDesc: "{title}" and its messages are deleted. The agent, its memory and its workstation stay.

model.title: Default model
model.description: Agents think with this model unless they're configured with their own. Any provider/model pair works, including local models.

localModels.title: Local models
localModels.description: Run agents for free on this computer. Download a model with one click and make it the default.

providers.title: Model providers
providers.description: Bring your own keys. Configure as many providers as you like and mix them across agents. Local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio) need only an endpoint.

integrations.title: Workstations & web
integrations.description: Agents' machines run in Docker on this computer. Firecrawl is optional: without it agents search and read the web only by browsing.

vault.title: Vault
vault.description: What agents may use on your behalf — encrypted here, never shown to them.

remoteAccess.title: Telegram
remoteAccess.description: Talk to your agents from anywhere. Chuck Bot polls Telegram from this machine — no public URL, no port forwarding, no tunnel.

system.title: System
system.description: Where your data lives and what Chuck Bot is running on.

thread.screenshotAfterNotKept: Screenshot after this step not kept.
thread.takeOverHint: Do your part, then hand it back — it carries on from there.
thread.takeOverFromThread: Take over from this agent's own thread (Screen tab), then reply here when you're done.
thread.screenAfterAction: The screen just after this action

templates.title: Templates
templates.description: Ready-made agents with standing orders for common jobs. Pick one to open it in the editor: rename it, change its orders or give it its own model before it goes online. Each gets its own desktop and memory, like any agent.

routines.title: Routines
routines.description: Tasks your agents do on their own, on a schedule: a news brief every morning, job alerts on weekdays, a price check every evening. They run on this computer while Chuck Bot is open, post into their own thread, and reach your phone through Telegram if it's connected.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Every agent turn is recorded locally: the model it ran on, the tokens it consumed and what that cost. Local models are free. Your providers bill you directly — Chuck Bot just keeps the receipts.
usage.nothingYet: Nothing yet. Talk to an agent and its turns land here.

notFound.title: Nothing out here.
notFound.description: The agent, squad or thread you're looking for doesn't exist — it may have been deleted.
